content: Before birth, an obstetric ultrasound scan can be utilized to screen pregnant women for indications of congenital heart disease (CHD) in their unborn babies. This screening is typically conducted around the 20th week of pregnancy, as the rapidly moving structures of the fetal heart are sufficiently developed and large enough to be visualized more clearly at this stage. If CHD is suspected during this initial screening, the mother is referred for a fetal echocardiogram. This is a more detailed and diagnostic ultrasound examination performed by a specialist cardiologist. Advancements in medical technology now allow specialists to screen for CHD as early as the 14th week of pregnancy, particularly if there are other factors that raise suspicion, such as a family history of congenital heart disease.
